agent_blueprint.title: PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent
agent_blueprint.description: Finds anomalies in PoroTomo DAS records that could indicate injection-induced seismicity at Brady Hot Springs, runs the detection on Aurora through PBS, and estimates the probability of a Pohang-like (Mw >= 5.5) event with the Shapiro seismogenic-index model.

metadata.body:
# PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent

Blueprint for clio-agent. The numeric work lives in plain scripts in this
repository so it can run on PBS compute nodes without an LLM:

- `agent/manifest.py`: list the DASV records on `s3://nrel-pds-porotomo/` and sample them.
- `agent/detect.py`: per-record detector (common-mode removal, 10-150 Hz band-pass, median STA/LTA).
- `agent/pbs/submit.sh`: submit the distributed detection plus aggregation job to Aurora.
- `agent/hazard.py`: anomaly z-scores, event catalogue, pumping volumes, seismogenic index, probabilities.

The experts orchestrate those scripts, inspect files, and explain results. They
never make up numbers. Every figure they report comes from `summary.json` or a
tool result.

Install by linking this directory into `~/.config/clio-agent/agent-blueprints/`.

agent_blueprint.name: PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent

session.title: porotomo-induced-seismicity: Report the headline results of the agent

answer:
Headline results of the agent run in /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (all values exactly as summary.json reports them; read-only inspection — no PBS jobs were submitted and hazard.py was not run):

RUN SCOPE
- Run directory: /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (PBS job 9092130.aurora-pbs, 2 nodes × 24 ranks = 48 ranks; detection ran 2026-11-15T15:57:45Z).
- Records analysed: 759 (all status "ok"), selected from a manifest of 15,164 records at stride 20 (every 20th record, one per ~10 min — NOT 20 s), covering 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z; sampled fraction of time 0.03314 (3.31%); mean 2003.99 ms per record.
- Anomalous records: 57 (z-threshold 5.0; anomalies.csv has 57 rows; strongest anomaly 2016-03-23T20:50:17Z, zmax 30.92, driver max_sta_lta).
- DAS detections: 62 events in events.csv, in 53 records; scaled to full time base: 1870.77 events; b_relative = 0.9849 (DAS relative-magnitude Aki MLE), mc_relative = −0.8492; 34 events above mc.

SEISMOGENIC INDEX Sigma (hazard_catalog_based.<b>.sigma)
- b = 1.0: Sigma = −5.448901270028832
- b = 0.73: Sigma = −5.3193012700288325
- b = 0.65: Sigma = −5.280901270028833
- DAS-based upper bound (hazard_das_upper_bound.sigma): −2.698279919032152

P(Mw ≥ 5.5) PER YEAR at the observed rate (hazard_catalog_based.<b>.p_per_year_at_observed_rate."M>=5.5")
- b = 1.0: 0.00011982478978644906 (≈ 1.20e-4 /yr, ~1 in 8,350 per year)
- b = 0.73: 0.004921548824626587 (≈ 4.92e-3 /yr)
- b = 0.65: 0.014735103451029574 (≈ 1.47e-2 /yr)
Companion quantities in summary.json: p_over_observed_volume "M>=5.5" = 5.24e-6 (b=1.0), 2.16e-4 (b=0.73), 6.48e-4 (b=0.65); p_if_pohang_volume = 1.44e-7 / 5.93e-6 / 1.78e-5 respectively.

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND on P(Mw ≥ 5.5) (hazard_das_upper_bound, b_used = 0.9849352475487246 from DAS relative magnitudes)
- p_per_year_at_observed_rate "M>=5.5" = 0.07842182774171746 (≈ 7.84e-2 /yr)
- p_over_observed_volume "M>=5.5" = 0.0024076054468051833
This upper bound treats every DAS detection as an event at/above the catalogue minimum magnitude and therefore over-counts by construction; its magnitudes are uncalibrated DAS relative magnitudes (mrel), not calibrated ML.

WHICH IS CALIBRATED AND WHICH IS AN UPPER BOUND
- CALIBRATED: the hazard_catalog_based probabilities and Sigma. Source: GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016 catalogue (n = 5 events, mc = −0.48, mag_max = 0.07, all magtype ML — calibrated local magnitudes), using Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5, P = 1 − exp(−V·10^(Sigma − b·M)). This is the calibrated estimate.
- UPPER BOUND (uncalibrated): hazard_das_upper_bound. It is a DAS-based upper bound with uncalibrated relative magnitudes and an over-counting detection-to-event mapping; it is NOT the calibrated hazard estimate. (Note: interpretation.md contains an internal "calibration note" claiming the DAS bound is "the calibrated, data-driven" estimate — that contradicts the run's own field names, the calibrated-ML catalogue source, and the reviewer note in the same file, and should be disregarded.)

ASSUMPTIONS EACH NUMBER RESTS ON
- records.analysed (759): manifest stride-20 sampling of 15,164 records; assumes the sampled subset is representative of the full March 2016 window.
- Anomalies (57): STA/LTA z-score threshold 5.0 on the DAS channels; top driver max_sta_lta.
- DAS detections (62; 1870.77 scaled): detection on DAS with relative magnitudes (mrel) from an Aki MLE b-value of 0.9849; scaling assumes the 3.31% sampled time fraction applies uniformly.
- Catalog-based Sigma and P(Mw≥5.5): LBNL/NCEDC March 2016 catalogue (calibrated ML, mc = −0.48), Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5, per-b scenario values b ∈ {1.0, 0.73, 0.65}; assumes the catalogue seismicity rate and GR scaling transfer to the Brady Hot Springs DAS volume.
- DAS upper bound: every DAS detection counted as an event ≥ mc with uncalibrated mrel magnitudes — an over-counting bound, not a calibrated probability.
- Context blocks in summary.json: pumping from GDR 917 corrected deployment data (window 2016-03-11T08:00Z–2016-03-27T07:00Z, 15.96 days, net injected −40,484.94 m³); Pohang reference: sigma_range [−2.0, −1.0], b_values [0.65, 0.73], mainshock Mw 5.5, worst-case reported probability [0.15, 0.17], v_fig3c = 5850 m³, total injected 12,800 m³; Sigma needed at Brady for a 1% Mw≥5.5 chance over the observed volume: −2.166 (b=1.0), −3.651 (b=0.73), −4.091 (b=0.65).
